title: Rental Period Continuity Values for PAP Therapy Equipment
content:
# Rental Period Continuity Values — PAP Therapy Equipment

Two events can interrupt a PAP Therapy Equipment rental: a break in need, when rental is suspended for a hospital or skilled nursing stay, and the start of payment by a different primary coverage. For each device class this reference fixes the days of a break in need, beyond the days left in the rental month in which it began, after which a new rental period must start; what a new rental period after such a long break needs before billing resumes; and what a patient already on therapy needs when a new primary coverage starts paying mid-rental.

| Device class | Break in need (days) | New rental period after a long break needs | New primary coverage mid-rental needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Travel CPAP System (E0601) | 0 | not applicable | not applicable |
| CPAP Fixed-Pressure System (E0601) | 60 | a new order and a new practitioner visit | the qualifying test on file and a new practitioner visit |
| Auto-Adjusting CPAP System (E0601) | 60 | a new order and a new practitioner visit | the qualifying test on file and a new practitioner visit |
| Bilevel PAP Spontaneous System (E0470) | 60 | a new order and a new practitioner visit | the qualifying test on file and a new practitioner visit |
| Bilevel PAP Spontaneous-Timed System (E0471) | 60 | a new order and a new practitioner visit | the qualifying test on file and a new practitioner visit |
| Adaptive Servo-Ventilation System (E0471) | 60 | a new order and a new practitioner visit | the qualifying test on file and a new practitioner visit |

## Notes

- The Travel CPAP System (E0601) is never rented, so no break-in-need figure and no requalification applies to it.
- The 60 days of a rented class are added to the days remaining in the rental month in which the suspension began; the sum is the allowance within which the patient's return home keeps the same rental period.
- "The qualifying test on file and a new practitioner visit" means that the qualifying sleep test already on file predates the new coverage and that a new practitioner visit documents continued use and benefit.

**Example (hypothetical).** A CPAP Fixed-Pressure System (E0601) rental is suspended with 12 days remaining in the rental month in which the suspension began. The allowance is 60 plus 12, or 72 days.
